newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda president urges Zaires Mobutu to negotiate.
newsitem.headline: Uganda president urges Zaires Mobutu to negotiate.

text.p: Uganda's President Yoweri Museveni urged President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire on Thursday to negotiate with rebels Kinshasa says are backed by Ugandan troops.
"I think the situation really is serious in Zaire for the Mobutu government and I think what he should do is negotiate with this armed opposition," Museveni told a news conference.
"There is definitely political frustration and I think it is good for Marshal Mobutu to notice this and negotiate with the opposition," said Museveni, a former rebel leader who seized power in 1986.
Asked about external influence on the war in eastern Zaire, the Ugandan leader said those in Rwanda opposed to the late president Juvenal Habyarimana had found allies in Zaire and vice versa.

Habyarimana, a member of the Hutu majority, was killed on April 6, 1994, triggering the genocide of an estimated 800,000 people by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs until Tutsi-led rebels, backed by Uganda, seized power three months later.
Zaire has repeatedly accused Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of sending troops to fight alongside the rebels in eastern Zaire. All three of Zaires eastern neighbours deny doing so.
